observation.visible_scene: A dark violet-to-black backdrop with a soft, brighter purple glow concentrated in the upper-center and a few faint vertical light streaks. The frame is filled with numerous small pink, magenta and violet particles that look like out-of-focus dots and short vertical streaks (petal- or bokeh-like), scattered across the whole image with a denser, brighter cluster near the top-center glow.
visible_changes: The particle field drifts slowly and continuously downward throughout the excerpt; many particles that sit higher in early frames (e.g., the bright dot near the left-middle and the dots around the central glow) appear progressively lower in later frames, and several elongated streaks indicate vertical motion.
Individual particles change brightness from frame to frame (twinkling): some dots brighten to a near-white core while others dim or vanish, without the whole field uniformly changing.
There is slight lateral wobble in some particles' paths as they fall, but the overall pattern of motion is vertical descent rather than sideways translation.
The upper-center glow and the faint vertical background streaks stay in roughly the same positions across all frames, indicating the background/light source is stationary relative to the camera.
No new object enters from a specific edge and no object is seen to land or stop; particles near the top and bottom edges are simply part of the same drifting field, consistent with a mid-action crop.

The bright cluster near the top-center remains the most luminous region over time, with particles within it continuing to fall away and be replenished by particles arriving from above the visible top edge.
The density and arrangement of particles change continuously but the total number visible stays roughly constant, suggesting a steady flow rather than a burst or fade-out.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the particles actually are (petals, confetti, dust, light motes, or a rendered effect) and what caused them to start falling.
The source of the purple glow and vertical streaks (a light fixture, a window, or a background texture).
Whether the motion continues, accelerates, or stops beyond the last frame, and what preceded the first frame.
The true depth/scale of the particles and whether apparent size differences reflect distance or just blur.
uncertain_details: Whether the small horizontal shifts of some particles are genuine lateral drift or a very slight camera movement; the fixed background streaks argue against major camera motion but a tiny pan/zoom cannot be excluded.
Whether a given bright dot in one frame is the same physical particle as a nearby dot in the next (twinkling and overlap make identity ambiguous).
The exact speed of the descent, since only sparse time samples are provided.
Whether the elongated streaks are motion-blurred dots or distinct elongated objects.

Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
